evals.prompt: I want to build a new Power Platform ToolBox tool that lets me bulk-update Dataverse records from a CSV file.
evals.expected_output: Should first check whether the current directory already looks like a PPTB tool project (package.json with displayName/main/icon, @pptb/types in devDependencies) and, since it doesn't, proceed with scaffolding. Should ask the developer which framework to build with via AskUserQuestion, presenting the four sample-tools options (HTML/vanilla TS, React, Vue, Svelte) with their stack and best-for guidance. Should not proceed to run the generator until a framework is chosen.
assertions: Checks for an existing PPTB tool project before scaffolding (Step 0)
Asks which framework to use via AskUserQuestion rather than assuming one
Presents all four sample-tools options (HTML, React, Vue, Svelte) with stack and best-for guidance
Does not run the Yeoman generator before a framework is chosen

evals.prompt: Create a new PPTB tool using React called bulk-updater.
evals.expected_output: Should recognize that the framework (React) is already stated and skip the AskUserQuestion framework prompt. Should proceed directly to running the Yeoman generator (`npx --package yo --package generator-pptb -- yo pptb bulk-updater`, or the globally-installed equivalent), selecting React when the generator itself prompts for a framework.
assertions: Skips the framework question since React was already stated
Runs or describes running the yo pptb generator with the given tool name
Carries the React choice into the generator's own framework prompt
Does not ask a redundant framework question

evals.prompt: Set up a new tool for the toolbox.
evals.expected_output: Should detect in Step 0 that `package.json` already has `displayName`, `main`, and `icon`, and that `@pptb/types` is already a devDependency. Should NOT re-scaffold or overwrite the existing project. Should tell the user this looks like an existing PPTB tool and point them at the sibling skills (add-toolbox-api, add-dataverse-api, add-powerplatform-api, configure-csp, validate-pptb-tool, publish-pptb-tool) instead.
assertions: Detects the existing manifest fields and @pptb/types dependency
Does not re-run the generator or overwrite existing files
Tells the user this looks like an already-scaffolded PPTB tool
Points to at least one relevant sibling skill instead of re-scaffolding

evals.prompt: Scaffold a new PPTB tool called icon-picker and show me the package.json you'd generate.
evals.expected_output: Should produce a package.json containing the required fields: name (scoped), version, displayName, description, main (index.html), icon (an SVG path relative to dist, not iconURL), license, contributors, and configurations.repository. Should explicitly avoid emitting the deprecated `iconURL` field under `configurations`. Should mention making the SVG theme-aware with fill="currentColor" or stroke="currentColor". Should only include features.minAPI if a specific API version dependency is identified, not by default.
assertions: Includes all required manifest fields (name, version, displayName, description, main, icon, license, contributors, configurations.repository)
Does not emit the deprecated iconURL field under configurations
Mentions fill="currentColor" or stroke="currentColor" for theme-aware icons
Does not add features.minAPI without a stated reason tied to a specific API version

evals.prompt: I'm porting my XrmToolBox tool 'Bulk Data Updater' to Power Platform ToolBox. I'm not the original author. What should I do?
evals.expected_output: Should surface the community etiquette note: since the developer isn't the original author, they should reach out to the original XrmToolBox author first as a courtesy before publishing a port. Should mention this is expected community practice, not a legal requirement. Should still proceed with the normal scaffolding steps (framework choice, generator, manifest, type definitions, starter) alongside the etiquette guidance, and may mention the PPTB Discord as a place to discuss the port.
assertions: Surfaces the etiquette note about contacting the original XrmToolBox author
Frames it as community courtesy, not a legal requirement
Still proceeds with the normal scaffold workflow (framework choice, generator, manifest, etc.)
May mention the PPTB Discord community as a discussion resource

evals.prompt: I don't have Node/npx available on this machine. Can you set up the files manually for a Vue-based tool called quick-notes?
evals.expected_output: Should recognize that the generator can't be run and fall back to a manual scaffold, creating the same file layout by hand (package.json, index.html, styles.css, app.ts/app.vue, README.md as applicable to Vue). Should point the developer at the vue-sample/ folder in the sample tools repository (https://github.com/PowerPlatformToolBox/sample-tools) as a working reference to copy patterns from. Should still complete the manifest and type-definition steps despite the generator being unavailable.
assertions: Recognizes the generator is unavailable and switches to a manual scaffold
Creates the same file layout by hand rather than blocking on the missing generator
References the vue-sample/ folder in the sample tools repository as a reference implementation
Still completes the package.json manifest and @pptb/types installation steps

evals.prompt: Build me a PPTB tool that also needs to read Dataverse account records and show them in a grid.
evals.expected_output: Should scaffold the tool (framework choice, generator, manifest, type definitions, starter) but should NOT attempt to implement the Dataverse grid/query logic itself. Should defer the actual Dataverse API wiring to the add-dataverse-api sibling skill, mentioning it explicitly in the hand-off, rather than writing dataverseAPI calls inline as part of this skill.
assertions: Completes the scaffold (framework, manifest, type defs, starter) as its own scope
Does not implement Dataverse query/grid logic itself
Explicitly defers Dataverse API wiring to the add-dataverse-api skill
Keeps the starter code limited to the generic connection-check/notification pattern, not business logic

evals.prompt: I'll go with the HTML Sample option — I just want plain TypeScript, no framework overhead. Call the tool 'env-badge'.
